newsitem.title: USA: Pa. considers bill limiting tax refunds -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Pa. considers bill limiting tax refunds -- paper.

text.p: If the Pennsylvania Supreme Court declares the personal property tax unconstitutional, a new bill would allow counties to keep any taxes collected in the years before the court rules, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Monday.
Under current state law, taxpayers can seek refunds for up to three years when a tax is declared unconstitutional. The bill would limit refunds to the year in which the tax is struck down.

The Senate has already passed the proposal as part of a sweeping tax reform bill designed to give local governments the option of reducing real estate taxes and levying an income tax, the newspaper said.
Billionaire Walter Annenberg is challenging Montgomery County's personal property tax, which raised $27.5 million in 1996. Montgomery and several other counties stopped collecting the tax in 1997.

The tax is levied on stock holdings in companies not registered in the state. The U.S. Supreme Court struck down a similar tax in North Carolina, saying it violated the Constitution's Commerce Clause.
